Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 50-year-old man with 5-day history of cough, coryza, low-grade fevers/sweats and new mild shortness of breath; likely viral upper respiratory infection, safety-net with delayed antibiotics.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Feeling generally unwell for 5 days with cough (mainly dry, minimal sputum), runny nose, sore throat, mild shortness of breath.
- Associated symptoms: Intermittent fevers/chills, night sweats, nasal congestion, mild ear dullness, generalized myalgia/arthralgia, 1 day of self-limited diarrhea; no chest pain, nausea or vomiting; appetite preserved, maintaining fluids.
- Onset/progression: Began Saturday (≈5 days ago) after evening out; symptoms persistent.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension.
- Medications: Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented; Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented; occasional aspirin – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Social history: Lives with wife; factory worker (steel parts). Alcohol ~9 pints beer/week. Cutting down on cigarettes, uses vaporizer. No children at home.

Examination:
- Telephone consult; no vitals recorded.
- Clinician noted audible nasal congestion (“sniffles”).

Impression:
- Probable viral upper respiratory tract infection/early influenza.
- Mild shortness of breath but no features of pneumonia at present.

Plan:
- Conservative management: rest, maintain hydration, regular Paracetamol for fever/discomfort.
- Delayed antibiotic prescription: Amoxicillin 1 tablet three times daily to start if no improvement or worsening in 24–48 h.
- Safety-netting: Seek review sooner for worsening breathlessness, high fever, chest pain, or other concerns.
- Follow-up: Telephone or in-person review next week if symptoms persist despite above measures.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected: objective vitals, physical examination, recent glucose/BP control, vaccination status, COVID screening, detailed medication doses.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational digressions but clinically adequate.
